items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I sang a song made popular on the radio by a guy named Skinnay Ennis... I thought, oh, I’ll sing this song.

ctx.x: Well, I wish we could talk all night here. I wish you the best of luck in your future project, and I can’t wait to read your book.

Oh, yes. That’s going to be interesting. I’m dredging up things that I had completely forgotten about you know. Like I forgot that I had worked with Art Tatum until I started to think about this book. I never told anybody that. I forgot about it. And there’s one really funny incident that I remember, it’s really, it’s funny but it’s also kind of poignant you know. But it also points out the philosophy that we had as my father’s children, you know. Like he was a very spiritual man and he taught us that we were…

living God. And every man, woman and child on this planet were our brothers and sisters. And never mind that they didn’t feel that way, that was their problem. It was our job to remember that we are brothers and sisters to every human being. So I find it solved all the racial problems I might have had. Because I’ve never really had any. You know, anybody comes to me, I give them the love I would give a brother. So if they have animosity toward me, first it’s got to get through that. And that’s pretty hard. That’s…
